Subject: Post-call recap: Exec summary & procurement path — Redwood <> AuroraMed

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick exec-friendly recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Attendees: Emily (AuroraMed), Chris (AuroraMed), Phil (not on call but exec sponsor), Sean (Redwood), Laura (Redwood), Marissa (Redwood).

Key business goals / outcomes
- Reduce per-query inference cost by ~30–40% to enable scaling call volume for clinical triage workflows.
- Improve tail latency to <200ms for the patient-summary endpoint (currently ~450ms).
- Maintain strict PHI controls and region-based data residency for US-only workloads.

Top pain points discussed
- Current vendor has high per-token cost and opaque billing spikes on peak traffic.
- Latency and variability impacting clinician experience.
- Procurement and security: need SOC 2 evidence, DPA language, and a predictable procurement path for a pilot.

Risk / escalation items for execs
- If procurement timeline slips >6 weeks, risk to Q2 pilot start and board-approved pilots.
- Phil (CTO) flagged model output consistency for clinical safety — suggested a short eval + quality gate.

Procurement path & timeline
- Emily indicated internal budget approval target: by 2027-04-15.
- Procurement will own MSA review (procurement@auroramed.com) + legal review of DPA.
- Proposed pilot: 8-week eval focused on two production endpoints; target pilot start week of Apr 11.

Next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Sean: Share mutual action plan (MAP) + high-level pricing and pilot scope (attached) — delivered (see attachments).
2) Emily: Introduce Phil/Finance if required for budget sign-off — requested.
3) Marissa: Prep pilot onboarding checklist & sample runbook (will follow up once pilot is confirmed).
4) Procurement: Confirm MSA review timeline and any required contract redlines.

Attachments: AuroraMed_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf (MAP), redwood-pricing-proposal-auroramed.xlsx (pricing).

If helpful, I can also schedule a 20‑minute exec intro with Phil and our VP of Product to walk the pilot success criteria and risk mitigations.

Thanks — Sean

--
Sean Gallagher

Thanks Sean — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Budget/Timeline: We are aiming for internal budget approval by 2027-04-15. If we can lock scope and pilot pricing by 4/1 that substantially increases the chance we hit the Apr 11 start.
- Procurement: looping in procurement@auroramed.com for MSA/DPA review. They will want SOC 2 Type II and a DPA template up front.
- Exec sponsor: Phil (CTO) is available for a 30-minute intro call week of Mar 29; that would be helpful to cover safety/quality gates and success metrics.

Also: Can you share a one-pager SLA or sample uptime/latency commitments we can share with legal? And if possible, a short note on how Redwood handles PHI/encryption in transit and at rest.

Couple follow-ups from Chris:
- Will you be able to run a short quality eval on a redacted sample? Phil wants to see a 500-case randomized pass/fail for our key summaries.

Appreciate the MAP and pricing — I’ll review with procurement and loop back with any redlines.

— Emily
